issues.title: Egypt Permanently Lists Muslim Brotherhood as Terrorist Entity, Official Gazette Says
issues.title_en: Egypt Permanently Lists Muslim Brotherhood as Terrorist Entity, Official Gazette Says
issues.summary: Egypt has permanently designated the Muslim Brotherhood as a terrorist entity, ending the possibility of the group’s listing expiring under previous time-limited court rulings, according to a decision published in the Official Gazette on Monday, 9 November . The decision, issued by the Office for Regulating Lists of Terrorist Entities and Terrorists at the Public Prosecution, also adds three individuals to Egypt’s terrorist list following final and binding court convictions. The three individuals named in the decision are Abdel-Rahman Hassan Mohamed Meligy, Gamal Abdel-Hamid Gomaa Abdel-Hamid, and Osama Ibrahim Mohamed Mostafa El-Rakh. The permanent designation follows several previous court decisions extending the Brotherhood’s classification as a terrorist organisation. Most recently, in December 2025, a court renewed the group’s designation for another five years. Under Egypt’s Law No. 8 of 2015 regulating terrorist entities and terrorists, listing an organisation carries a series of legal consequences, including prohibiting its activities, closing its premises, banning its meetings, and freezing its assets. The legislation also prohibits providing financial support to the organisation or collecting money and other resources on its behalf, whether directly or indirectly.
